summary.text: A 48-year-old man with a 15-year history of well-controlled HIV infection presented with mild elevation of liver enzymes on regular check-up. He was on highly active retroviral therapy and had a history of didanosine for 6 years. Hepatitis panel was negative and alpha-fetoprotein was less than 5 ng/mL.

Ultrasound and triple-phase CT showed two liver lesions, a noncirrhotic liver with splenomegaly and varices, and significant portal hypertension. A targeted biopsy showed a well-differentiated hepatocellular neoplasm; immunohistochemistry favored inflammatory-subtype hepatocellular adenoma and the nonneoplastic parenchyma was suggestive of hepatoportal sclerosis. Hepatic venous pressure gradient was 2 mmHg.

Two years later he was self-referred to a Transplant Center with a MELD score of 6, and an uncomplicated open right hepatectomy was performed without blood products. The postoperative course was uneventful and he was discharged home 4 days later. Pathology showed two well-differentiated hepatocellular carcinomas, margin-free and without vascular invasion; the nonneoplastic parenchyma was normal without significant fibrosis.
He has been followed up for 18 months and remains tumor-free.
